_meta.title: The court in residence at Persepolis (setting 'Court calendar = seasonal pattern' only; D-003, D-182): who, how many, where on the Terrace, and the rules of their days
_meta.tiers: A attested / B inferred (Greek claims about the Persian court are capped at B; search extracts are capped at B) / C reconstructed. EVERY count below is C: a derivation to meet population.json zones.terrace.court_resident (w 5,000 by day, 2,500 by night), sized in the proportions the sources give where they give any. Every place is C.
_meta.setting: The court in residence is the DEFAULT (UD-10, D-236; settings courtCalendar 'seasonal'): one residence a year in spring, the court arriving on the seed's day in the first weeks of Nisannu (courtYear.ts) and leaving on day 117 (E-26, month 4 day 29); a new game begins at its coming (D-239). The court-absent world remains only as the out-of-world setting 'evidence' (Q-005, B9). D-780: the court's programme (ceremony) runs every day of the residence.
_meta.king: D-199: with the setting the king IS a person (B9, Q-335): Xerxes on the reliefs' ceremonial dress (the Persian robe, the crown, the long beard, the staff and the lotus: B), walking from the Hadish to the Apadana with a parasol bearer and a fly-whisk and towel bearer behind him (the door-jamb reliefs: B) and four spearmen of his escort, enthroned there for an audience on about two mornings in five (C), and otherwise inside the Hadish, not drawn (seclusion, brief 9.1; C). D-780: he also rides out, hunts, stands before the magi's fire and presides over the great banquets (ceremony). Only the out-of-world 'evidence' setting (no court) has no king (Q-005).
placeholders: the royal guard's golden-apple spear butts are not modelled apart from the ordinary spear prop
music of the royal women at night (ATH12-HERACL) is not performed: they are shown awake with the lamps
the delegations' animals, chariots and the carried lioness, and the mantles, shawls and tassels of some peoples, are not modelled (delegations.json notes)
the king's walk: his parasol and fly-whisk bearers walk their own routes at his hour, not locked in step behind him
the camps' tents have no colliders: the visitor walks through them; the paths between the tents are straight lines
_meta.filled_d199: D-199: delegation dress (delegations.json, the Apadana reliefs: form B, colours C), the king (B9, Q-335), the camps' tents (camps.ts: C) and the retinue in the town and on the plain (Q-333: C) are built

resident.note: D-252: first_day is no longer read: the court ARRIVES on a seed-chosen day (arrival below; courtYear.ts) and is resident from then to last_day; it leaves on leave_day (E-26, month 4 day 29)

arrival.note: D-252: ONE residence a year, in spring: the court comes from Susa on a day the seed draws in the first weeks of Nisannu (window, day of the regnal year; day 0 = 1 Nisannu) and leaves on E-26's day. Basis: Persepolis a spring/summer residence of a mobile court (WP-PERS-SEASON, tertiary; RESIDENCE2021, abstract: B for the pattern, C for any year); trips to the king peaking at the New Year under Darius (KING2022, B); Xenophon's claim that the king spent the spring at Susa (Cyr. 8.6.22, a claim about Cyrus, B) puts Susa on the road before; the PF Susa-Persepolis road (ROYALROAD-GIS, B) is the road it comes by. Nothing places Xerxes at Persepolis in 467 (Q-005). The window starts after day 5 so that the arrival has a before inside the simulated year; nearest the New Year the year's window allows (C; Q-680). Two residences a year: nothing in research/ supports a second stay (rejected, Q-680). The order of coming (the household ahead to make ready, a first part of the guard, heralds on the road, the baggage the day before, the king's column, the camp followers after: every day and hour C, Q-681)
arrival.king_note: the king reaches the road station at this hour of his day and walks up with the parasol over him (the door-jamb reliefs, B; the arrival on foot C: no chariot or carriage is drawn, a placeholder: Q-682)
arrival.start_note: D-239: a new game (a fresh seed, no ?day and no save) begins at dawn (sunrise - 0.4 h, civil dawn at 30 N, C) 1-3 days (the seed's draw) before the seed's arrival day; any date can still be chosen
arrival.entry_note: everyone of the court comes in along the royal road from the W (the Susa road, settlement.json road_royal_west: C course) and is first seen at the state stable that stands in for the road station (town.json station, D-043), 1.8 km W of the Grand Stair; from there on foot (or riding, the heralds) to the camps and up the Grand Stair. Beyond the station they are not drawn (the land beyond has no places yet: Q-683). Leaving, they go down the same way and are last seen there
arrival.groups_note: the household that keeps the palaces and the king's table comes four days ahead to make ready: the halls swept, the kitchens and the table store stocked from the royal stores, the flocks for the table penned at the stockyard (C); the first two hundreds of the king's spearmen three days ahead to take the posts (C); the rest on the king's day, the spearmen at the head of the column, the officials and the Persians of rank before the king, the women of the household and their attendants after him (C). Hours are when each household reaches the road station
arrival.retinue_note: the baggage, the supply trains, the herds and the horses come the day before the king and pitch their camps (C); the soldiers in the town lead the column and those of the plain close it; the servants of the Persians of rank come with their masters' baggage in the afternoon; the craftsmen and sellers who follow a court the day after (C). A camp's tents are pitched by its households as they come (camps.ts pitch), not standing before

heralds.note: T-F5: news of the court travels ahead of it by couriers of the royal road (the relay of HDT 8.98 and XEN-CYR 8.6.17-18, claims: B; the PF 'express messenger', pirradaziš: B): two a day in the four days before the king, riding in along the royal road, taking the word up to the officers at the Gate of All Nations, a night at the road station and away W again to meet the column the next morning (all C)

arrival.visitors_note: petitioners and delegations come from the second day of the residence (C: they come to a king who is there)

camp.note: the court's lodging below the Terrace on open ground NW of its foot, between the approach road and the north official complex. The retinue 'lodged or camped' in the town (population.json town court_resident, C); where is not known (Q-333). Tents: camps.ts (D-199)

camps.label: the court's camp below the Terrace
camps.note: the court's own people who do not sleep on the Terrace, and the petitioners and delegations; tents in lines facing the Terrace (E), the nobles' and officials' larger tents nearest the centre (C). Persian tents: HDT 9.70, 9.80 (claims about an army, B); on the march the army camped in the open air (HDT 7.119): tents for all is C

camps.label: the retinue's camp NW of the official building
camps.note: open ground N of the official quarter (C; Q-333)

camps.label: the retinue's camp W of the Terrace's S end
camps.note: open ground between the lower town and the royal stores (C; Q-333)

camps.label: the retinue's camp NW of Persepolis West
camps.note: open ground between the craft quarter and the road station (C; Q-333)

camps.label: the retinue's camp SW of Persepolis West
camps.note: open ground W of the lower town (C; Q-333)

camps.label: the royal horse lines on the plain
camps.note: grooms and herdsmen of the court's horses and mules, on open ground toward the river (C; Q-333)

camps.label: the supply trains' camp by the royal road W
camps.note: the drivers of the grain, wine and fodder trains (C; Q-333)

camps.label: the soldiers' camp S on the plain
camps.note: soldiers who came with the court and are not on the Terrace (HDT 7.41, 7.83: the ten thousand with the king, a claim about an army on the march: B; their camp here C)

groups.label: the king's spearmen (the thousand 'apple-bearers', mēlophoroi)
groups.note: HDT 7.41 (a claim about Xerxes' army on the march): a thousand spearmen with golden pomegranates on the spear butts inside nine thousand with silver ones; HDT 7.83: the Ten Thousand 'Immortals'. Heracleides of Cyme (via Athenaeus 12.514b-c; SX): a thousand 'apple-bearers', Persians of rank chosen from the Ten Thousand, guard the king. Both B as claims; the thousand in residence at Persepolis in 467 is C. Persian and Median dress alternate as on the Apadana and Tripylon reliefs (B). Organised as ten hundreds of ten files of ten (HDT 7.81 decimal units, B claim) on the garrison's five-day watch cycle (D-023, C); sleeping in the garrison quarters with the Terrace garrison (capacity unknown: Q-331)

groups.label: the women of the king's household
groups.note: Heracleides (via Athenaeus 12.514b; a claim about Artaxerxes II): three hundred women who sleep by day and keep watch at night with singing and lamps; Parmenion's letter (Athenaeus 13.608a; Darius III's baggage at Damascus, 333): 329 concubines skilled in music. Both B as claims; 300 in 467 is C. Secluded in the building Herzfeld called the Harem (the name and use are debated: Q-334), never out on the Terrace (C)

groups.label: attendants of the royal household (eunuchs and women servants)
groups.note: the Treasury audience relief shows a beardless attendant (read as a eunuch) with a towel behind the throne (SX, B); eunuchs at court (IR-COURT, SX, B). The men wear the Persian robe as on the reliefs; the number is C

groups.label: palace servants: sweepers, water carriers, keepers of the halls
groups.note: no count is known; the Terrace's halls kept by a staff that also serves when the court is away (the palace caretakers, population.json) grows with the court (C)

groups.label: the king's table: cooks, bakers, wine and water staff, servers
groups.note: the proportions follow Parmenion's list (B claim, Darius III): 277 cooks, 29 pot boilers, 13 dairy cooks, 17 drink makers, 70 wine strainers, 40 perfumers, 46 garland weavers; the Greek claims that the king's table fed 15,000 a day (Ctesias and Dinon via Athenaeus 4.146c; SX) and Heracleides' account of the royal dinner (Athenaeus 4.145-146) are claims (B); PF 0701, 126,100 qa of flour 'consumed before the king' (Darius, SX, B). The royal kitchens are NOT located on the Terrace: placed on the open ground W of the Hadish and S of the Tachara (C, Q-332)

groups.label: the supply line: porters carrying up from the royal stores
groups.note: the royal stores that receive grain, wine and figs (PF, Darius era, B) supply the table; the porters and their loads are C

groups.label: butchers of the royal table at the stockyard
groups.note: slaughter at the stockyard is attested (PF 58-60, A, Darius era); 'a thousand animals slaughtered for the king every day' is a Greek claim (Athenaeus 4.145e; SX, B) and is NOT the rate used: the count of butchers is C

groups.label: officials, secretaries and ushers of the court
groups.note: the hazarapatiš ('chiliarch') commands the thousand and screens visitors before an audience; an usher (Greek eisangeleus) announces them (IR-CHIL, SX, B). Ushers lead delegates by the hand on the Apadana reliefs (B). Secretaries: the Elamite and Aramaic chancery (LANGUAGES, B). The Tripylon as the officials' place is C (its use is debated)

groups.label: Persians of rank in attendance (the king's table-companions among them)
groups.note: 'table-companions' (homotrapezoi) as a court title (SX, B); Persian and Median nobles in the Apadana processions (B imagery); the number in attendance is C

visitors.label: petitioners and gift-bearing delegations waiting on the king
visitors.up_note: D-221: on a day that is not its audience a party goes up to wait in the forecourt with this chance (C; was 0.6 before D-221), and only while the forecourt has a place for it (waiting.stations, waiting.line): the rest wait at the camp

waiting.note: D-221: 25 places of the forecourt for delegations (blocks of five abreast, 0.9 m apart, rows 1 m deep, facing the N stair), W and E of the way between the files of spearmen, nearest the stair first; petitioners in lines of 31 along the E side facing the stair (a second line beside the first when it is full; a party is not split); in the hall the parties called next stand in blocks facing the throne, between the columns; each party goes before the king in turn (at most a quarter of an hour, the morning's parties in the order they came), led up from the forecourt 0.3 h before its turn by an usher who has stood at its head from 0.75 h before. All C: the reliefs give the form (an usher leading each delegation: B), nothing gives the places or the hours

visitors.origins_note: D-199: the 23 peoples of the Apadana delegations (delegations.json); a party brings its own people's gifts and wears its own dress
visitors.note: the Apadana reliefs show 23 delegations in their own dress bringing gifts, each led by an usher (B for the types). Whether they show a real annual procession is debated (brief section 2): D-780 stages the days of the peoples' gifts all the same (the reliefs as the programme; C). Parties come on their own days (C), wait at the Gate and in the forecourt, and are led up to the Apadana on the day of their audience; petitioners come in ones and twos (C). D-780: on the days of the peoples' gifts every delegation at Persepolis goes up in the reliefs' order (court.json ceremony; UD-09, UD-10, UD-29 overrule 'no procession is staged'). 'Trips to the king' at the New Year (KING2022, Darius era, B for the pattern) and gifts of the peoples (HDT 3.97, claim) support their presence, not their numbers (C)

king.label: the king (Xerxes) with his parasol bearer, his fly-whisk and towel bearer and four spearmen of his escort
king.note: Nothing places Xerxes at Persepolis in 467 (Q-005): he is here only because the setting places the court here (C). His dress, crown, beard, staff and lotus, and the two attendants behind him, are as the door-jamb reliefs of the Tachara and the Hadish carve them (HADISH-JAMB, B: an image of royal ceremony); the audience enthroned with a footstool, the towel bearer behind the throne (TREAS-AUD, B). The Hall of a Hundred Columns is a building site in 467 (D-003): the audience is held in the Apadana (C). How often he gave audience, at what hour and where the throne stood are C (two mornings in five, from about 08:30 for two hours or so). The escort: the king's spearmen about him (Xenophon Cyr. 8.3: a claim about Cyrus, B; four men C). Otherwise he is inside the Hadish and is not drawn (seclusion: brief 9.1; C). He never speaks to or reacts to the visitor (brief 1.1); D-780: the court's programme (ceremony) has him enthroned on the days of the gifts, riding out, hunting, at the fire and presiding over the banquets (UD-09, UD-10, UD-29).

retinue.label: the court's retinue lodged in camps in the town and on the plain
retinue.note: population.json: town + 8,000-20,000 'lodged or camped' and plain + 3,000-10,000 'in supply trains, royal herds and camps' with the court resident (C derivations). Who they were is not recorded for Persepolis: the servants of the Persians of rank, grooms and horse lines, the baggage and supply trains, craftsmen and sellers who follow a court, and soldiers (HDT 7.41, 7.83; Athenaeus 4.145-146 on the court's size: claims, B). Every count, group, camp and day rule is C, sized so that the town and the plain hold population.json's court-resident working values (tests/court.test.ts); they lodge in camps of tents (camps.ts), not billeted in the town's houses (billeting is not modelled: C).

guard_lines_note: Ceremonial posts (C): files of ten standing where the reliefs put guards (stairways, gates, façades: B for the motif) and along the processional ways; a file holds one stretch of ten posts for a watch and moves to another the next time (C). D-221: the posts of a line stand file_spacing_m apart, centred on the line (a line of 20 is two files of ten shoulder to shoulder), every man facing the line's heading, not strung out along its whole length (the reliefs' guards stand in close files: B for the motif; the spacing C). By night only the stair head, the Gate, the palaces and the Tripylon are held (C); the rest of the night watch waits within call at the guards' court

day.file_spacing_note: D-221: a man's width with his shield and bow case, arms' length apart (C; the reliefs carve the spearmen overlapping in profile)
day.note: walking at 1.25 m/s over 1.3 × the straight line, +10 min to climb to the Terrace (as lives.json walk_ms); each man at a post is relieved once in his watch for a meal, two of a file of ten at a time (C)

ceremony.note: D-780 (UD-09, UD-10, UD-29 overrule 'no procession is staged'): the court's recurring events as simulation, not cutscenes: a pure function of the seed and the day (ceremony.ts). The Apadana reliefs are the programme: delegations in their peoples' dress led by ushers with their gifts and animals (APA-RELIEF, B for the form); the king enthroned with the chiliarch before him, his hand raised to his mouth (TREAS-AUD, IR-CHIL: B); the king's table and his banquets (Heracleides in Athenaeus 4.145-146, a claim: B; Parmenion's list of the king's musicians and cooks, Athenaeus 13.608: B claim); gifts and sacrifice when the king comes to Persia (Xenophon Cyr. 8.5.21: a claim, B); the king's birthday feast, the tukta (Herodotus 9.110: B claim); the king's ride out of the palace with the chariot, the horses and the spearmen (Xenophon Cyr. 8.3: a claim about Cyrus, B); the hunt (Cyr. 1.4, 8.1.38: B claim); the relay of mounted couriers (Herodotus 8.98: B claim). The New Year's trips to the king (KING2022, B pattern). Every day, hour, count and place is C.

gift_days.note: the days of the peoples' gifts: the first a few days after the king comes (the New Year, KING2022: B pattern), then every ten to sixteen days; every delegation then at Persepolis goes up in the reliefs' order, each behind its usher, with its gifts and animals; more parties come in the days before one (C)

ride.note: on a morning without an audience the king rides out from the palace down the Great Stair and over the plain to the royal horse lines and back, his spearmen and the parasol about him, Persians of rank riding behind, grooms with led horses (Cyr. 8.3: a claim, B; C)

hunt.note: the king's hunt on the plain and the foot of the hills N of the royal horse lines: the king and Persians of rank on horseback, beaters and grooms on foot, out at first light and back after midday (Cyr. 1.4, 8.1.38: B claims; C)

banquet.note: great banquets in the Apadana: the night after the king comes (his gifts to the Persians), every day of the peoples' gifts, the king's birthday and about one night in seven besides; the Persians of rank and the senior officials at low tables between the columns, the king's servers carrying the dishes over the Terrace from the kitchens, lamps on stands, the king at the head of the hall under the canopy (Heracleides: a claim, B; the Book of Esther 1: late, C)

birthday.note: the tukta, the king's birthday feast (HDT 9.110: B claim): the king anoints his head and gives gifts to the Persians; its date is unknown and drawn from the seed within the residence (C)

couriers.note: royal-road couriers riding in to the road station at the gallop with letters for the court and riding out again at dawn (the relay: HDT 8.98, a claim, B; horse rations POTTS2023: B; the count C)

exercise.note: the grooms exercising the court's horses at the horse lines morning and evening, ridden at a trot in strings and led (C)

guard_change.note: the watches of the king's spearmen change at 06, 14 and 22 (garrison cycle D-023: C); the relieving files march out of the guards' court to their posts

dawn_rite.note: the magi's fire fed before first light and the day's offering (E-30, D-209); on the morning after the king comes and on his birthday the king stands before the fire with the barsom-bearing magi (the tomb reliefs of Naqsh-e Rustam: the king before the fire altar, B; C)

chiliarch.note: the chiliarch (hazārapatiš) standing before the throne at an audience, his right hand raised before his mouth, presenting those called (TREAS-AUD: the figure before the king, B; IR-CHIL: B; C)

feast_hall.note: the Apadana's hall (site_spec apadana hall_side 60.5, hall_centre, interaxial 8.25: C/B) laid with low tables in the bays between the columns, the diners seated round them; the throne bays and the carpet road from the N door kept clear (C)
